affiliations.date_precision: The scholarly chronology places factory work in 1942-1943 immediately before OSS service beginning in 1943; no factory name or exact transition date is supplied.
affiliations.research_notes: The source explicitly sequences 1942-1943 factory work before 1943-1946 OSS and State Department service. The employer remains unnamed and is not normalized to a candidate company.

affiliations.date_precision: The exact Army-entry record carries civilian occupation code 727 and records Army entry on February 24, 1941. No start date is documented.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms identity and places the grouped occupation at Army entry. The category does not identify an employer, worksite, exact trade, or Army-to-OSS chronology.

affiliations.date_precision: The institutional finding aid says Cassady returned to France in 1942 as naval attaché and then reported to OSS; no exact transfer date is supplied.
affiliations.research_notes: This is a military diplomatic assignment immediately preceding the documented OSS reporting relationship, not a civilian employer.

affiliations.date_precision: The finding aid says Cassady worked as an investor before and after World War II but supplies no employer, business name, dates, or employment arrangement.
affiliations.research_notes: Investor is published only as a prewar occupation. The evidence does not establish self-employment, a firm, or the last civilian employer before wartime service.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Johann Caspari is a high-confidence match to the German social-policy official later known as Hans and John Caspari.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A university-published biography uses the exact indexed name, documents Hans and John variants, and places him in OSS service from 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The uncommon exact name, documented variants, and explicit OSS chronology provide multiple corroborating identifiers beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source dates factory work to 1942-1943 and OSS or State Department service to 1943-1946.
claims.match_notes: No private identifier is printed in the index. Box 112 remains the strongest route to confirmation.

claims.claim_text: Johann Caspari worked as a factory worker in New York in 1942-1943 immediately before his documented OSS service began in 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The scholarly chronology places unnamed factory employment directly before service in OSS and the State Department.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The claim belongs to the high-confidence exact-name OSS identity.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded and sequential, but the exact transition date and factory name are not documented.
claims.match_notes: The public profile must say unnamed factory and must not invent or normalize an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Gino H. Cassai is confirmed as the same enlisted soldier represented in the official Army merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The OSS index and official Army file agree on the exact name and private identifier.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact private-identifier agreement across two official NARA records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record documents entry on February 24, 1941 but not the later OSS transfer.
claims.match_notes: The private identifier is withheld. The Army grade supports enlisted classification only.
